content.title: A look at Ole Miss basketball coach Chris Beard
content.text: Ole Miss men’s basketball vs. Oklahoma at the Sandy and John Black Pavilion in Oxford, Mississippi. Saturday, March 1, 2025. No. 4 Tennessee basketball will head to Oxford on Wednesday to play the Ole Miss Rebels. Ole Miss was an underperforming basketball program under head coach Kermit Davis. After a 74-79 career record in Oxford, Davis was fired during the 2022-23 season. Chris Beard was hired after the season to replace Davis as the Rebels’ head coach. Beard’s coaching career Beard is a disciple of Hall of Fame coach Bob Knight and his son Pat Knight while they coached at Texas Tech. Beard worked as an assistant and associate head coach of the Red Raiders until 2011. He took on various head coaching positions in the American Basketball Association and Division II basketball before getting hired as the head coach of the Little Rock Trojans. Beard spent one season at Little Rock and clinched a bid to the 2016 NCAA Tournament. Beard and the Trojans upset fifth-seed Purdue in double overtime before losing to Iowa State in the Round of 32. Beard returned to Texas Tech in 2016, this time as a head coach. He racked up awards and accomplishments as the coach of the Red Raiders. He coached Texas Tech to its first ever Elite Eight in 2018, and its first ever national championship game appearance in 2019. Beard won AP Coach of the Year in 2019. Beard left Texas Tech for Texas, his alma mater, in 2021. He continued his success by leading the Longhorns to their first NCAA Tournament win since 2014. Beard’s career in Texas was cut short by controversy. After leading the Longhorns to a 7-1 record in his second season, Beard was arrested for assault. Although the charges were dismissed and Beard acted in self-defense, it cost him his job. As the Rebels’ head coach Two months after being fired by Texas, Beard took the job to become the Ole Miss head coach. He instantly improved the Rebels in his first year, as they were ranked in the AP Poll for the first time since 2019. Ole Miss started this season ranked and rose up to No. 16 before dropping six of its last 11, causing them to become unranked. The Rebels have wins over Alabama and Kentucky this season. Beard quoted his former mentor Knight, after the Kentucky win. “That’s Bob Knight,” Beard said. “Victory favors the most aggressive team, and the team with the fewest mistakes.” Ole Miss has six players averaging over 10 points per game. Beard only inherited one starter when he took over in 2023. He recruited the other four from the transfer portal, including Sean Pedulla, the Rebels leading scorer. Beard adds to the long list of legendary coaches that Tennessee has played this year. The Vols have played Scott Drew, John Calipari and Bruce Pearl, beating two of the three. Playing against a coach like Beard, with a history of NCAA Tournament success, will be important for the Vols with only two games left of the regular season. The No. 4 Vols look to extend their winning streak to five, while the Rebels are playing for a higher seed in the SEC and NCAA Tournament.
